newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Market speculation often wrong on rulings-ACCC.
newsitem.headline: Market speculation often wrong on rulings-ACCC.

text.p: Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) Chairman Alan Fels on Friday remarked that the stock market had a "particularly inaccurate" record in speculating on the outcome of decisions of the anti-monopolies watchdog.
Shares in Westpac Banking Corp rose sharply on Thursday and Bank of Melbourne shares fell as speculation grew that the ACCC would not approve their A$1.435 billion merger.
"It's just premature and the stock market tends to speculate in a particularly inaccurate manner on forthcoming ACCC decisions," Fels told reporters.

"For once I'm not going to, perhaps, accept too much blame for that. I suggest that the stock market is excessively prone to speculative behaviour just on wisps of information, rumours and idle gossip," he said.
Fels said earlier that the market assessment on the Westpac-Bank of Melbourne was premature.
Fels said the anti-monopolies authority's probe on the merger was focused on transaction accounts and the ACCC did not have concerns about the implications of the merger on the home loan market.
Westpac shares were steady at A$7.20 at 11.40 a.m. (0140 GMT), while Bank of Melbourne shares were 15 cents higher at A$9.10.
